sample_unit: anonymized orofacial pain patient case descriptions

links.outcome: GPT4 diagnostic accuracy versus clinical experts, medical students, and general practitioners on the same 24 cases
links.effect: GPT4 was comparable to non-expert evaluators but surpassed by clinical experts, who correctly diagnosed 54% of cases at ICOP level 3; GPT4 reached level 3 in 38% of the 100 cases.
links.quote: In the subset of 24 cases, the model's performance was comparable to non-expert human evaluators but was surpassed by clinical experts, who correctly diagnosed 54% of cases at level 3.

links.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of GPT4 primary and differential diagnoses against gold-standard diagnoses
links.effect: Overall diagnostic score was 157/300 (52%); differential diagnoses were accurate in 80% of cases (400/500 points).
links.quote: The model provided accurate differential diagnoses in 80% of cases (400 out of 500 points).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4 on retrospective clinical case descriptions of orofacial pain compared to human evaluators, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
